subject: Draft order form: IP ownership, training permissions and feedback license
messages:
From: Claire Park <claire.park@amplify.ai>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: Dan Liu <dan.liu@amplify.ai>
Date: Mon, 01 Jul 2029 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Draft Order Form - IP & Training Clause Questions

Hi Karthik,

Thanks for sending over the draft order form yesterday. Procurement/legal here at Amplify flagged a few items we need clarity on before we can move to signature:

- Output ownership: The redline appears to assign output rights to the customer in some places and to Redwood in others. Can you confirm the default position and point to the specific language we should expect in the final order form?

- Training/data use: There is a proposed clause that would allow Redwood to improve models using customer prompts and outputs. Amplify cannot agree to training on customer prompts or generated outputs without explicit opt-in. Are you able to remove any automatic training rights, or provide a narrow telemetry/feedback-only license?

- Feedback license: We are open to a limited feedback/telemetry license for product improvements, but need concrete exclusions for PII and a clear deletion/segregation mechanism.

I attached a marked-up order form (AMPL_OrderForm_redline.docx) with our comments. Can we schedule a short call this week to resolve the above? Our legal lead (Dan) is copied.

Thanks,
Claire Park
Senior Counsel, Amplify AI
claire.park@amplify.ai

-----
Attachment: AMPL_OrderForm_redline.docx (redline of order form; comments on sections 2.1, 7.3, Exhibit A)

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: Claire Park <claire.park@amplify.ai>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 01 Jul 2029 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Draft Order Form - IP & Training Clause Questions

Claire — thanks for the redlines and the clear asks. Looping in Laura (legal) and Marissa (CS) to align on product/ops constraints.

Preliminary answers before we sync:

- Output ownership: Our standard is that customers retain ownership of their content and outputs they generate from their prompts. We will mark the order form to reflect "Customer retains title to Customer Content and Outputs." We do need a narrow right to reproduce outputs for troubleshooting if the customer requests support.

- Training/data use: We understand the sensitivity here. Redwood does not train production models on customer data by default unless there is an explicit opt-in in the order form. That said, our defaults in the platform allow collection of anonymized telemetry to detect regressions and performance issues. We can propose language that: (a) prohibits model retraining without an opt-in checkbox on the order form; and (b) limits automatic data collection to aggregate/non-attributed telemetry (no prompts or outputs).

- Feedback license: We can accept a narrowly scoped feedback license limited to non-personal, aggregated telemetry and tooling metrics; we will exclude prompt/response text unless the customer explicitly tags data for improvement. We will also add retention/deletion commitments.

I've attached a short text file with proposed clause language (Proposed_clause_text.txt) for legal to review. Can we book 30 minutes Wednesday (preferably 9:00am PT) for a quick walkthrough?

—Karthik Iyer
Account Lead, Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Phone: +1 415-555-0123

-----
Attachment: Proposed_clause_text.txt (draft language for Section 7.3 and Exhibit A)

From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
To: Claire Park <claire.park@amplify.ai>, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 03 Jul 2029 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Draft Order Form - IP & Training Clause Questions

Claire / Karthik — Laura here (Legal). Thanks for the clear redline. I reviewed Karthik's proposed language and have three legal items we should align on: 

1) No assignment of pre-existing rights: We'll confirm that Redwood does not claim title to Customer's pre-existing content. Insert explicit language: "Customer retains all right, title and interest in Customer Content and Customer Outputs."

2) Training / Model Improvement: We can agree to the opt-in approach. We propose the following contract structure:
   - Core clause in the MSA/order form: "Redwood will not use Customer Content or Customer Outputs to train, fine-tune, or improve models unless the parties execute an explicit training addendum."
   - Separate Feedback License: allow a non-exclusive, worldwide, royalty-free license to use aggregated, de-identified telemetry for product improvement. Redlines: exclude prompt/response pairs; exclude any data flagged as Sensitive; require data minimization.

3) Audit, deletion and evidence: Amplify requests the ability to audit or receive evidence of deletion/segregation of data used for improvements. We can offer quarterly attestation of data handling and a documented deletion workflow, and carve out audit rights to the extent permitted by Redwood's platform/security constraints.

I'll propose concrete contract language in track changes; please confirm the timing for an internal Amplify sign-off on the opt-in approach so I can finalize the clauses.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
General Counsel, Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.ai

-----
(Internal note: Marissa, can you confirm the operational steps for attestation and how we surface deletion evidence to the customer?)

From: Claire Park <claire.park@amplify.ai>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: Dan Liu <dan.liu@amplify.ai>
Date: Thu, 04 Jul 2029 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Draft Order Form - IP & Training Clause Questions

Laura / Karthik — thanks for the quick follow-up and for separating the training addendum approach — that addresses a lot of our concerns. A few Amplify procurement/legal points in response: 

- Absolute prohibition on training without opt-in: We require explicit contractual language that Redwood "shall not" use Customer Content or Customer Outputs for model training, fine-tuning, or evaluation absent a signed training addendum. The word "shall" is important to our procurement counsel.

- Feedback/telemetry license: We can accept a limited telemetry license for product improvement, but it must: (a) explicitly exclude prompt and output text; (b) exclude any content marked as Sensitive; and (c) include a retention cap (e.g., telemetry retained no longer than 90 days unless explicitly consented).

- SLA/regressions: Amplify needs a concrete operational remedy if a model change introduced by Redwood causes measurable regressions on our account. Can you add a clause offering credits or rollback rights in the training addendum? Procurement will not sign without a remediation path.

I've attached a purchase order draft (PO_Amplify.pdf) with our procurement timeline; we need final language this week to hit July 15 procurement window.

Best,
Claire Park
Senior Counsel, Amplify AI

-----
Attachment: PO_Amplify.pdf (procurement timeline and PO template)

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: Claire Park <claire.park@amplify.ai>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 08 Jul 2029 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Draft Order Form - IP & Training Clause Questions

Claire / Dan — thanks, and appreciate the procurement timeline. Summary and proposed compromise below to keep us on schedule: 

1) Ownership: Redwood will include explicit language: "Customer retains all right, title and interest in Customer Content and Customer Outputs." We'll remove any ambiguous assignment language.

2) Training: Redwood confirms we will not use Customer Content or Customer Outputs to train, fine-tune, or otherwise improve any production models unless Amplify signs a separate training addendum that explicitly lists datasets and scope. We'll add the mandatory "shall not" phrasing requested.

3) Feedback license & telemetry: Redwood will accept a narrowly scoped feedback license limited to aggregated, de-identified telemetry for product improvements only. We will expressly exclude prompt/response text and any data Amplify marks as Sensitive. Proposed telemetry retention: default 90 days; extended retention only via explicit consent. We will add a deletion workflow and quarterly attestation to satisfy audit needs.

4) SLA / regressions: For cases where Redwood's changes cause measurable regressions impacting Amplify's production KPIs, Redwood will provide a remediation path: credit equal to X% of monthly fees for the impacted period and an operational rollback option where technically feasible. Laura will work with Claire to finalize appropriate credit benchmarks and rollback conditions.

Next steps:
- Laura to provide final redline language by tomorrow EOD (we will aim to incorporate into the order form).
- Karthik to generate a tracked PDF of the agreed sections and upload to HubSpot + DocuSign prep.
- Claire / Amplify to confirm if they will sign the training addendum when ready or push to a later PO cycle.

I'll upload the final redline package here: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1a2b3c-amplify-orderform-redline and create the DocuSign envelope once we have Laura's language. If this timeline looks good, we'll aim to finalize before July 15.

Thanks all — appreciate the quick turnaround.

—Karthik Iyer
Account Lead, Redwood Inference
